title: Billy Strayhorn's ticket and Billie Holiday closing the concert
summary: Jumping ahead, he tells of Strayhorn sending him to a concert with Ellington, Parker with strings and Stan Getz, where Billie Holiday's closing set silenced the room.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: So that was another aspect of sound. Now I start thinkin', you know. And then, another time, there was Billy Holiday. I'll never forget, I was at the Paradise, so Billy Strayhorn says, "Nick, I got a ticket for you and I want you to come to this concert." I says, "Look, ya know I'm workin' here and whatnot and they mad if I turn around." You know, they want to make this money, 'cause we was doin' very well. So I just said, "O.K." So, let me tell you what happened, man. So I got there, so that meant I had to be at my job later on, but I didn't even care, 'cause Billy Strayhorn say, "You gotta go." 'Cause he lived right up the street from the Paradise and he used to bring all his friends from all over the world into the Paradise to see me.
Yeah, well, yeah, yeah. Wait a minute now you made me lose my point there.

Yeah. Oh yeah, yeah. So I went to the concert and...I tell you what happened. Duke Ellington's Band...Charlie Parker and strings, Stan Getz and Billie Holiday closed the show. So I sit up there and listened to all this wonderful music and, when they finished, Billie Holiday got up there and started singin', it was like you had never heard anything all night. I says, 'My God!' So, hahaha, I'm tellin' ya, everybody was speechless, I'm tellin' ya. She just took out everything. You forgot anything that happened before; when she got through it was all over. I'm tellin' ya. And everybody knew it too. And I'm young and I really knew it, you know. Shoot. And the old timers that knew her, shoot, they weren't even worried about it, but it was a shock to me. A sound. So all these things come together. That's what helped me, you know, try to get this sound that I'm tryin' to get, you know, but it's not perfect and I work on it all the time, you know. Yeah.
